name: WorkOS
abstract: Developer-first B2B identity platform from the USA designed for SaaS companies adding enterprise features. Flagship products include Enterprise SSO (SAML/OIDC with 20+ IdP integrations), Directory Sync (SCIM from Okta, Entra ID, Workday, Google Workspace), AuthKit (hosted login UI with passkeys and social login), Fine-Grained Authorization (hierarchical RBAC/ReBAC), Radar (bot and fraud protection), and Vault (BYOK encryption). Free up to 1 million MAUs. SaaS-only deployment.

plans.name: Free
plans.price: Free (up to 1M MAUs; includes AuthKit, SSO, Directory Sync)

plans.name: Audit Logs
plans.price: $125/month per SIEM connection or $99/month per million events

featureList.description: Google, Microsoft, GitHub, Apple, GitLab, LinkedIn, Slack, and Xero. Configured per-application in the WorkOS Dashboard.

FIDO2/WebAuthn passkeys supported as both first and second factor via AuthKit. Passkeys satisfy MFA requirements since they require biometric or device PIN verification. Progressive enrollment prompts password users to register a passkey on next sign-in. Passkeys are bound to the custom domain; only available through AuthKit hosted UI.
Magic Auth sends a six-digit one-time code to the user's email inbox. Codes expire after 10 minutes. Configurable via WorkOS Dashboard and customizable email templates.
WorkOS does not support SMS-based passwordless authentication. By design, SMS is excluded because it is a phishable authentication method.
WorkOS Magic Auth uses a six-digit OTP code sent by email, not a clickable magic link. Clickable link-based authentication is not available.
WorkOS requires authenticated user identity. Anonymous or guest session flows are not a built-in feature.
Time-based OTP via any TOTP-compatible authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Authy, etc.). Configurable and resettable via the User Security Widget.
WorkOS only supports TOTP (time-based OTP). Counter-based HOTP is not available.
Roaming FIDO2 security keys (YubiKey, etc.) supported as a second factor through the WebAuthn/Passkeys implementation.
WebAuthn/Passkeys satisfy both first and second factor requirements. Platform authenticators (Face ID, Touch ID, Windows Hello) and roaming security keys are supported.
Email OTP is available as a first-factor passwordless method (Magic Auth), but not as a standalone MFA second factor.
WorkOS explicitly does not offer SMS MFA by design, citing SMS as a phishable authentication method that weakens the authentication chain.
Backup codes generated at MFA enrollment for account recovery when the primary MFA device is unavailable.
WorkOS does not have a proprietary push notification MFA app. Passkeys provide a comparable user experience for tap-to-approve flows.
WorkOS does not offer risk-based or adaptive MFA. Authentication policies are configured statically per application.
No native Cisco Duo MFA integration. WorkOS supports Duo as an Enterprise SSO identity provider (SAML/OIDC), but not as a Duo-specific second-factor provider.
WorkOS does not have a built-in step-up authentication mechanism. Re-authentication flows would need to be implemented at the application layer.
WorkOS acts as an OIDC provider via WorkOS Connect. Supports authorization code flow with PKCE, token introspection, and standard discovery.
WorkOS can act as a SAML 2.0 Identity Provider through WorkOS Connect, in addition to supporting SAML as a Service Provider (Enterprise SSO). Supports both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows.
WorkOS does not support WS-Federation. Microsoft Entra ID and ADFS are supported via SAML 2.0 and OIDC connections.
OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials grant for service-to-service authentication. M2M tokens support API authorization for backend services and agentic workflows.
Per-organization OIDC SSO connections for enterprise customers. Supports Okta, Google, PingIdentity, Generic OIDC, and many others. IT admins can self-configure connections via the Admin Portal.

Per-organization SAML 2.0 SSO connections. Supports Okta, Azure AD, ADFS, Google Workspace, JumpCloud, OneLogin, PingFederate, and 20+ enterprise IdPs. SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows supported. Admin Portal enables self-service setup.
WorkOS does not support native LDAP or Active Directory protocol. On-premises AD is integrated via SCIM provisioning or SAML/OIDC federation, not direct LDAP.
Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) supported as both an SSO provider (SAML/OIDC federation) and a Directory Sync source via SCIM.
Bulk user creation and import via the User Management API. Migration tooling supports importing users at scale from external systems.
Import users with existing password hashes during migration. Supported algorithms include bcrypt, scrypt, argon2i, argon2id, MD5, SHA-1, and PBKDF2.
Export users via the User Management API with pagination and filtering support.
Individual user update and delete operations are supported via the API. No dedicated bulk batch endpoint; bulk operations require iterating through the API.
User import API supports upsert semantics for migration scenarios.
MFA enrollments (TOTP secrets, WebAuthn credentials) cannot be imported. Users must re-enroll MFA after migrating to WorkOS.

Directory Sync: enterprise identity providers (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Workday, JumpCloud, and any SCIM 2.0-compliant directory) push user and group changes to WorkOS via SCIM 2.0.
WorkOS does not push user changes to downstream third-party applications as a SCIM client. WorkOS delivers directory sync events to your application via webhooks and the Events API.
Directory Group sync is supported. Group membership changes from enterprise IdPs are delivered via Directory Sync events and available via the Groups API.
Just-in-time user provisioning creates WorkOS user records on first SSO login without pre-provisioning via Directory Sync.
WorkOS provides migration tooling for gradual user migration from legacy systems, including password hash import and API-driven user creation that avoids forced password resets.
AuthKit provides a built-in User Security Widget for end-user MFA management and account security settings. Profile management available via AuthKit hosted UI.
Multiple authentication methods (social, enterprise SSO, passkeys) can be linked to a single user account.
Users can be deactivated via the User Management API to prevent all sign-in.
Custom user-editable metadata stored per user via the User Management API.
Application-managed, non-user-editable metadata on user objects via the API.
Metadata limits are documented in the WorkOS developer reference.
Search and filter users by email, organization, and other attributes via the User Management API.
Role-based access control via the Roles API. Roles can be assigned to users within organizations, and WorkOS FGA extends this with hierarchical resource-scoped permissions.

Organizations are a first-class B2B multi-tenancy primitive in WorkOS. Each organization can have dedicated SSO connections, Directory Sync, domain verification, member management, and Admin Portal access.
Password strength and complexity requirements configurable per application via the WorkOS Dashboard.
Username and email format restrictions configurable per application.

PassKey progressive enrollment prompts users to adopt stronger authentication on subsequent sign-ins. Full progressive profiling forms for collecting arbitrary user attributes are not a built-in feature.
WorkOS does not have a built-in ABAC policy engine. Attribute-based rules can be implemented at the application level using user metadata from WorkOS.

WorkOS FGA extends RBAC with hierarchical, resource-scoped access control. Subjects (users/groups), resources (workspace, project, document), and privileges (roles/permissions) support inheritance down the resource hierarchy, sharing conceptual similarities with Zanzibar-style ReBAC.
OAuth 2.0 scopes and permissions for API access control via WorkOS Connect. M2M Client Credentials flow for backend service authorization.
WorkOS can sign Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) for customers under enterprise plans.
User data exportable via the User Management API for GDPR portability requests.
Users can be permanently deleted via the User Management API to satisfy GDPR right to erasure.
WorkOS does not have a built-in consent management or privacy consent feature. OAuth 2.0 scopes provide basic consent screens for WorkOS Connect applications.

WorkOS infrastructure is primarily US-based. Personal data transferred outside the EEA is stored in the US. BYOK Vault allows encryption keys to remain in specific cloud regions (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Google Cloud KMS).
WorkOS is a SaaS-only platform with no self-hosted or on-premises deployment option.
Audit Logs product captures authentication and administrative events with configurable retention. Available as a separate paid add-on ($99/month per million events).
Audit Logs can be streamed to external SIEM systems. $125/month per SIEM connection.
WorkOS does not provide a dedicated threat monitoring dashboard. Security analytics are available via Radar reports and the Audit Logs product.
All data encrypted at rest. WorkOS Vault uses envelope encryption with Data Encryption Keys (DEK) and Key Encryption Keys (KEK).
All endpoints enforced over TLS. SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configured automatically for email authentication.
WorkOS Vault supports Bring Your Own Key (BYOK). Customers provide encryption keys managed in AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or Google Cloud KMS. WorkOS access is scoped and auditable.
WorkOS Radar provides bot, fraud, and abuse detection for authentication flows. First 1,000 checks included free; $100/month per 50,000 additional checks.
Automatic account lockout and rate limiting on authentication endpoints to prevent brute force attacks.
WorkOS Radar detects and throttles suspicious sign-in attempts from anomalous IP addresses as part of fraud protection.
WorkOS does not provide dark web credential monitoring.
WorkOS does not expose device fingerprinting as a standalone feature. Radar handles bot and fraud detection at the network/request level.
Admin Portal supports per-organization branding. AuthKit supports application-level branding customization (logo, colors, domain).
MFA enforcement can be configured per organization, requiring enterprise users to complete MFA based on their organization's policy.
AuthKit provides a fully hosted and customizable login UI (logo, colors, background image, custom domain). Handles all authentication flows including social login, passkeys, and Enterprise SSO.
AuthKit is primarily a hosted-redirect login experience. Embedding components directly in app UIs requires custom implementation using the WorkOS User Management API.
Custom domain ($99/month) and full branding customization (logo, colors, background) removes WorkOS branding from the AuthKit login experience.
AuthKit UI supports some localization capabilities. Full multi-language i18n support is not prominently documented.
AuthKit provides a hosted login UI with ready-to-use components for all authentication flows. Framework-specific integration guides available for Next.js, Remix, Astro, and others.
WorkOS Dashboard provides analytics for authentication events, active users, and SSO/Directory Sync connection activity.
Official SDKs for Node.js/TypeScript, Python, Ruby, Go, PHP, Java, and .NET. Framework-specific quickstarts for Next.js, Remix, Astro, Express, Laravel, Django, Rails, and more.
Comprehensive REST API for managing users, organizations, SSO connections, directory sync, roles, and all WorkOS resources.
WorkOS enforces rate limits on authentication API endpoints with documented limits per endpoint.
Webhooks deliver real-time events for authentication, user lifecycle, directory sync, and SSO changes to external endpoints. Events API provides pull-based event retrieval.
WorkOS does not provide a managed serverless runtime for hooks. Webhooks are dispatched to customer-hosted endpoints, which can be implemented in any language.
Custom domain for AuthKit login pages and authentication endpoints. Required for passkeys in production. Available as a paid add-on at $99/month.
WorkOS does not provide an official CLI for managing or deploying WorkOS configuration as code.
A community-maintained Terraform provider exists (osodevops/workos) supporting organization, user, SSO, and webhook management. No official WorkOS-published provider.
WorkOS does not support custom database connections or scripts for delegating authentication to a legacy credential store.
WorkOS pushes real-time events (authentication, directory sync, SSO lifecycle) to configured webhook endpoints with signature verification.
AuthKit hosted login page supports full visual customization: logo, background image, brand colors, and custom CSS via the WorkOS Dashboard.
WorkOS sends Magic Auth OTP emails automatically. Custom email templates are supported, but routing through a custom SMTP relay is not natively configurable.
Customizable email templates for Magic Auth OTP, MFA enrollment, and other transactional emails via the WorkOS Dashboard.
Custom claims can be added to WorkOS Connect access tokens and ID tokens via token configuration.
WorkOS does not provide a visual no-code authentication flow builder. Flows are configured via the Dashboard and API.
WorkOS does not offer document-based identity verification or biometric liveness checks.
WorkOS does not support W3C Verifiable Credentials or decentralized identity (DID) standards.
WorkOS does not include built-in billing or subscription management integration.

WorkOS Pipes provides app and agent integrations for AI workflows. M2M Client Credentials tokens support service-to-service and agent authentication. Dedicated MCP server authentication features are in early development.

No direct vendor claim of PQC TLS support, but WorkOS's published subprocessor list names Cloudflare, Inc. alongside AWS, and WorkOS's public API (api.workos.com) responds with 'server: cloudflare' and a cf-ray header, confirming Cloudflare fronts WorkOS's API traffic. Cloudflare enabled hybrid PQC key exchange by default for TLS 1.3 in 2023-2024 - infra-inherited, not a WorkOS-specific commitment.
No public evidence WorkOS supports ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, or FN-DSA for JWT/SSO token signing.

No dedicated PQC roadmap found. A WorkOS blog post about NIST standards mentions quantum computing once, in passing, as an example of a future threat NIST is addressing generally - no WorkOS-specific commitment, timeline, or crypto-agility claim.
No public evidence found that the provider supports ML-KEM or HPKE (RFC 9180) for encrypting JWE tokens, SAML assertions, or user secrets.
No public evidence found of post-quantum or hybrid X.509 digital certificate support for mTLS client authentication or federation endpoints.
No public evidence found of NIST SP 800-208 stateful hash-based signature scheme support (LMS/HSS, XMSS).
